articleTitle: Corrigendum: A geometric model for the module category of a gentle algebra
abstract: In this note we correct an oversight in [A geometric model for the module category of a gentle algebra, Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN 2021, no. 15, 11357–11392] regarding morphisms between indecomposable modules of a gentle algebra. The oversight only occurs when bands are involved, which can be easily corrected by considering infinite periodic strings associated to bands and the universal cover of the surface associated to the gentle algebra.

articleTitle: On Schrödinger Groups of Fractional Powers of Hermite Operators
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {H}=-\Delta + |x|^2$</tex> be the Hermite operator on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb R^n$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\ge 2$</tex>. In this paper, we prove the boundedness of Schrödinger groups of fractional powers of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {H}$</tex> on Lebesgue and Hardy spaces. More precisely, we prove that (a) for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p \in (1,\infty )$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma>0$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta /\gamma \geq n|1/p -1/2|$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$ \begin{align*} \big\|\mathcal{H}^{-\beta /2}e^{it \mathcal{H}^{\gamma /2}}f\big\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)} \leq C (1 + |t|)^{n|1/p-1/2|}\|f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}, \quad \forall t \in \mathbb{R}, \end{align*}$$</tex> and (b) for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p \in (0, 1]$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma>0$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta /\gamma \geq n(1/p -1/2)$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$ \begin{align*} \big\|\mathcal{H}^{-\beta /2}e^{it \mathcal{H}^{\gamma /2}}f\big\|_{H^p_{\mathcal{H}}(\mathbb R^n)} \leq C (1 + |t|)^{n(1/p-1/2)}\|f\|_{H^p_{\mathcal{H}}(\mathbb R^n)}, \quad \forall t \in \mathbb{R}, \end{align*}$$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^p_{\mathcal {H}}(\mathbb R^n)$</tex> is the Hardy space associated with the operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {H}$</tex>. These estimates improve related result of Thangavelu [22] and have some interesting applications.

articleTitle: Correction to: Spectrum of the Neumann–Poincaré Operator and Optimal Estimates for Transmission Problems in the Presence of Two Circular Inclusions
On the Lp Brunn-Minkowski theory and the Lp Minkowski problem for C-coconvex sets
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> be a pointed closed convex cone in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathbb {R}}^n}$</tex> with vertex at the origin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$o$</tex> and having nonempty interior. The set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A\subset C$</tex> is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>-coconvex if the volume of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> is finite and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A^{\bullet }=C\setminus A$</tex> is a closed convex set. For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0<p<1$</tex>, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-co-sum of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>-coconvex sets is introduced and the corresponding <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p$</tex> Brunn–Minkowski inequality for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>-coconvex sets is established. We also define the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p$</tex> surface area measures, for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0\neq p\in {\mathbb {R}}$</tex>, of certain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>-coconvex sets, which are critical in deriving a variational formula of the volume of the Wulff shape associated with a family of functions obtained from the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-co-sum. This motivates the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p$</tex> Minkowski problem aiming to characterize the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p$</tex> surface area measures of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>-coconvex sets. The existence of solutions to the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p$</tex> Minkowski problem for all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0\neq p\in {\mathbb {R}}$</tex> is established. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p$</tex> Minkowski inequality for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0<p<1$</tex> is proved and is used to obtain the uniqueness of the solutions to the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p$</tex> Minkowski problem for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0<p<1$</tex>. For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p=0$</tex>, we introduce <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(1-\tau )\diamond A_1\oplus _0\tau \diamond A_2$</tex>, the log-co-sum of two <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>-coconvex sets <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{1}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{2}$</tex> with respect to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau \in (0, 1)$</tex>, and prove the log-Brunn–Minkowski inequality of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>-coconvex sets. The log-Minkowski inequality is also obtained and is applied to prove the uniqueness of the solutions to the log-Minkowski problem that characterizes the cone-volume measures of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>-coconvex sets. Our result solves an open problem raised by Schneider [41].

articleTitle: The Farrell–Jones Conjecture for Hyperbolic-by-Cyclic Groups
abstract: We prove the Farrell–Jones conjecture (FJC) for mapping tori of automorphisms of virtually torsion-free hyperbolic groups. The proof uses recently developed geometric methods for establishing the FJC by Bartels–Lück–Reich, as well as the structure theory of mapping tori by Dahmani–Krishna.

articleTitle: On Semisimplicity of Jantzen Middles for the Periplectic Lie Superalgebra
abstract: We prove that an integral block of the category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal O$</tex> of the periplectic Lie superalgebra contains a non-semisimple Jantzen middle if and only if it contains a simple module of atypical highest weight. As a consequence, every atypical integral block of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal O$</tex> does not admit a Kazhdan–Lusztig theory in the sense of Cline, Parshall, and Scott.

articleTitle: A Separable Universal Homogeneous Banach Lattice
abstract: We prove the existence of a separable approximately ultra-homogeneous Banach lattice <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak {B}\mathfrak {L}$</tex> that is isometrically universal for separable Banach lattices. This is done by showing that that the class of finitely generated Banach lattices has the Amalgamation Property and thus form a metric Fraïssé class. Some additional results about the structural properties of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak { BL}$</tex> are also proven.

articleTitle: Sharp Decay Rate for the Damped Wave Equation With Convex-Shaped Damping
abstract: We revisit the damped wave equation on two-dimensional torus where the damped region does not satisfy the geometric control condition. It was shown in [1] that, for sufficiently regular damping, the damped wave equation is stale at a rate sufficiently close to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t^{-1}$</tex>. We show that if the damping vanishes like a Hölder function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|x|^{\beta }$</tex>, and in addition, the boundary of the damped region is locally strictly convex with positive curvature, the wave is stable at rate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t^{-1+\frac {2}{2\beta +7}}$</tex>, which is better than the known optimal decay rate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t^{-1+\frac {1}{\beta +3}}$</tex> for strip-shaped dampings of the same Hölder regularity. Moreover, we show by example that the decay rate is optimal. This illustrates the fact that the sharp energy decay rate depends not only on the order of vanishing of the damping but also on the shape of the damped region. The main ingredient of the proof is the averaging method (normal form reduction) developed by Hitrik and Sjöstrand ([20], [35]).

articleTitle: The Branch Set of Minimal Disks in Metric Spaces
abstract: We study the structure of the branch set of solutions to Plateau's problem in metric spaces satisfying a quadratic isoperimetric inequality. In our 1st result, we give examples of spaces with isoperimetric constant arbitrarily close to the Euclidean isoperimetric constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(4\pi )^{-1}$</tex> for which solutions have large branch set. This complements recent results of Lytchak–Wenger and Stadler stating, respectively, that any space with Euclidean isoperimetric constant is a CAT(<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0$</tex>) space and solutions to Plateau's problem in a CAT(<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0$</tex>) space have only isolated branch points. We also show that any planar cell-like set can appear as the branch set of a solution to Plateau's problem. These results answer two questions posed by Lytchak and Wenger. Moreover, we investigate several related questions about energy-minimizing parametrizations of metric disks: when such a map is quasisymmetric, when its branch set is empty, and when it is unique up to a conformal diffeomorphism.

articleTitle: Classification of Thompson Related Groups Arising from Jones Technology I
abstract: In the quest in constructing conformal field theories (CFTs), Jones has discovered a beautiful and deep connection between CFT, Richard Thompson's groups, and knot theory. This led to a powerful functorial framework for constructing actions of particular groups arising from categories such as Thompson's groups and braid groups. In particular, given a group and two of its endomorphisms one can construct a semidirect product where the largest Thompson's group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> is acting. These semidirect products have remarkable diagrammatic descriptions that were previously used to provide new examples of groups having the Haagerup property. They naturally appear in certain field theories as being generated by local and global symmetries. Moreover, these groups occur in a construction of Tanushevski and can be realised using Brin–Zappa–Szep's products with the technology of cloning systems of Witzel and Zaremsky. We consider in this article the class of groups obtained in that way where one of the endomorphism is trivial leaving the case of two nontrivial endomorphisms to a 2nd article. We provide an explicit description of all these groups as permutational restricted twisted wreath products where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> is the group acting and the twist depends on the endomorphism chosen. We classify this class of groups up to isomorphisms and provide a thin description of their automorphism group thanks to an unexpected rigidity phenomena.

articleTitle: Non-Hamiltonian Actions With Fewer Isolated Fixed Points
abstract: Inan earlier paper, the second author resolved a question of McDuff by constructing a non-Hamiltonian symplectic circle action on a closed, connected six-dimensional symplectic manifold with exactly 32 fixed points. In this paper, we improve on this example by reducing the number of fixed points. More concretely, we construct a non-Hamiltonian symplectic circle action on a closed, connected six-dimensional symplectic manifold with exactly <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2k$</tex> fixed points for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k \geq 5$</tex>.

articleTitle: On a Class of Orthogonal-Invariant Quantum Spin Systems on the Complete Graph
abstract: We study a two-parameter family of quantum spin systems on the complete graph, which is the most general model invariant under the complex orthogonal group. In spin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S=\frac {1}{2}$</tex> it is equivalent to the XXZ model, and in spin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S=1$</tex> to the bilinear-biquadratic Heisenberg model. The paper is motivated by the work of Björnberg, whose model is invariant under the (larger) complex general linear group. In spin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S=\frac {1}{2}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S=1$</tex> we give an explicit formula for the free energy for all values of the two parameters, and for spin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S>1$</tex> for when one of the parameters is non-negative. This allows us to draw phase diagrams and determine critical temperatures. For spin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S=\frac {1}{2}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S=1$</tex>, we give the left and right derivatives as the strength parameter of a certain magnetisation term tends to zero, and we give a formula for a certain total spin observable, and heuristics for the set of extremal Gibbs states in several regions of the phase diagrams, in the style of a recent paper of Björnberg, Fröhlich, and Ueltschi. The key technical tool is expressing the partition function in terms of the irreducible characters of the symmetric group and the Brauer algebra. The parameters considered include, and go beyond, those for which the systems have probabilistic representations as interchange processes.

articleTitle: Cubic and Quartic Points on Modular Curves Using Generalised Symmetric Chabauty
abstract: Answering a question of Zureick-Brown, we determine the cubic points on the modular curves <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_0(N)$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N \in \{53,57,61,65,67,73\}$</tex> as well as the quartic points on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_0(65)$</tex>. To do so, we develop a “partially relative” symmetric Chabauty method. Our results generalise current symmetric Chabauty theorems and improve upon them by lowering the involved prime bound. For our curves a number of novelties occur. We prove a “higher-order” Chabauty theorem to deal with these cases. Finally, to study the isolated quartic points on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_0(65)$</tex>, we rigorously compute the full rational Mordell–Weil group of itsJacobian.

articleTitle: Cohomological Blowups of Graded Artinian Gorenstein Algebras along Surjective Maps
abstract: We introduce the cohomological blowup of a graded Artinian Gorenstein algebra along a surjective map, which we term BUG (blowup Gorenstein) for short. This is intended to translate to an algebraic context the cohomology ring of a blowup of a projective manifold along a projective submanifold. We show, among other things, that a BUG is a connected sum, that it is the general fiber in a flat family of algebras, and that it preserves the strong Lefschetz property. We also show that standard graded compressed algebras are rarely BUGs, and we classify those BUGs that are complete intersections. We have included many examples throughout this manuscript.

articleTitle: K-Theoretic Hall Algebras of Quivers with Potential as Hopf Algebras
abstract: Preprojective K-theoretic Hall algebras (KHAs), particular cases of KHAs of quivers with potential, are conjecturally positive halves of the Okounkov–Smirnov affine quantum algebras. It is thus natural to ask whether KHAs of quivers with potential are halves of a quantum group. For a symmetric quiver with potential satisfying a Künneth-type condition, we construct (positive and negative) extensions of its KHA, which are bialgebras. In particular, there are bialgebra extensions of preprojective KHAs and one can construct their Drinfeld double algebra.

articleTitle: Fractional Leibniz Rules Associated to Bilinear Hermite Pseudo-Multipliers
abstract: We obtain a fractional Leibniz rule associated to bilinear Hermite pseudo-multipliers in the context of Hermite Besov and Hermite Triebel–Lizorkin spaces. As a byproduct, we show that the classes of bounded functions in these spaces (which include Hermite Sobolev and Hermite Hardy–Sobolev spaces) are algebras under pointwise multiplication. To obtain these results we develop appropriate decompositions for bilinear pseudo-multipliers and molecular estimates for certain families of functions in the Hermite setting.

articleTitle: Maximal Tori in HH1 and the Fundamental Group
abstract: We investigate maximal tori in the Hochschild cohomology Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\operatorname {HH}}^1(A)$</tex> of a finite dimensional algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>, and their connection with the fundamental groups associated to presentations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>. We prove that every maximal torus in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\operatorname {HH}}^1(A)$</tex> arises as the dual of some fundamental group of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>, extending the work by Farkas, Green, and Marcos; de la Peña and Saorín; and Le Meur. Combining this with known invariance results for Hochschild cohomology, we deduce that (in rough terms) the largest rank of a fundamental group of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> is a derived invariant quantity, and among self-injective algebras, an invariant under stable equivalences of Morita type. Using this we prove that there are only finitely many monomial algebras in any derived equivalence class of finite dimensional algebras; hitherto this was known only for very restricted classes of monomial algebras.

articleTitle: Prop of Ribbon Hypergraphs and Strongly Homotopy Involutive Lie Bialgebras
abstract: For any integer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>, we introduce a prop <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathcal {R}}}{{\mathcal {H}}} ra_d$</tex> of oriented ribbon hypergraphs (in which “edges” can connect more than two vertices) and prove that it admits a canonical morphism of props,<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$ \begin{align*} & {\mathcal{H}}\textit{olieb}_{d}^\diamond \longrightarrow {{\mathcal{R}}}{{\mathcal{H}}} ra_d, \end{align*}$$</tex> <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal {H}}\textit {olieb}_{d}^\diamond $</tex> being the (degree shifted) minimal resolution of prop of involutive Lie bialgebras, which is nontrivial on every generator of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal {H}}\textit {olieb}_{d}^\diamond $</tex>. We obtain two applications of this general construction. First we show that for any graded vector space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> equipped with a family of cyclically (skew)symmetric higher products, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$ \begin{align*} & \Theta_n: (\otimes^n W[d])_{{{\mathbb{Z}}}_n} \longrightarrow {{\mathbb{K}}}[1+d], \ \ \ \ \ n\geq 1, \end{align*}$$</tex> the associated vector space of cyclic words <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Cyc(W)=\oplus _{n\geq 0} (\otimes ^n W)_{{{\mathbb {Z}}}_n} $</tex> has a combinatorial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal {H}}\textit {olieb}_{d}^\diamond $</tex>-structure. As an illustration, we construct for each natural number <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N\geq 1$</tex> an explicit combinatorial strongly homotopy involutive Lie bialgebra structure on the vector space of cyclic words in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> graded letters, which extends the well-known Schedler's necklace Lie bialgebra structure from the formality theory of the Goldman–Turaev Lie bialgebra in genus zero. Second, we introduced new (in general, nontrivial) operations in string topology. Given any closed connected and simply connected manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> of dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\geq 4$</tex>. We show that the reduced equivariant homology <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar {H}_{\bullet }^{S^1}(LM)$</tex> of the spacej <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$LM$</tex> of free loops in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> carries a canonical representation of the dg prop <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal {H}}\textit {olieb}^\diamond _{2-n}$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar {H}_{\bullet }^{S^1}(LM)$</tex> controlled by four ribbon hypergraphs explicitly shown in this paper.

articleTitle: Deformed Polynuclear Growth in (1+1) Dimensions
abstract: We introduce and study a one parameter deformation of the polynuclear growth (PNG) in (1+1)-dimensions, which we call the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex>-PNG model. It is defined by requiring that, when two expanding islands merge, with probability <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex> they sprout another island on top of the merging location. At <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t=0$</tex>, this becomes the standard (non-deformed) PNG model that, in the droplet geometry, can be reformulated through longest increasing subsequences of uniformly random permutations or through an algorithm known as patience sorting. In terms of the latter, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex>-PNG model allows errors to occur in the sorting algorithm with probability <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex>. We prove that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex>-PNG model exhibits one-point Tracy–Widom Gaussian Unitary Ensemble asymptotics at large times for any fixed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t\in [0,1)$</tex>, and one-point convergence to the narrow wedge solution of the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang equation as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex> tends to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex>. We further construct distributions for an external source that are likely to induce Baik–Ben Arous–Péché-type phase transitions. The proofs are based on solvable stochastic vertex models and their connection to the determinantal point processes arising from Schur measures on partitions.

articleTitle: Stability of Peaked Solitary Waves for a Class of Cubic Quasilinear Shallow-Water Equations
abstract: This paper is concerned with two classes of cubic quasilinear equations, which can be derived as asymptotic models from shallow-water approximation to the 2D incompressible Euler equations. One class of the models has homogeneous cubic nonlinearity and includes the integrable modified Camassa–Holm (mCH) equation and Novikov equation, and the other class encompasses both quadratic and cubic nonlinearities. It is demonstrated here that both these models possess localized peaked solutions. By constructing a Lyapunov function, these peaked waves are shown to be dynamically stable under small perturbations in the natural energy space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^1$</tex>, without restriction on the sign of the momentum density. In particular, for the homogeneous cubic nonlinear model, we are able to further incorporate a higher-order conservation law to conclude orbital stability in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^1\cap W^{1,4}$</tex>. Our analysis is based on a strong use of the conservation laws, the introduction of certain auxiliary functions, and a refined continuity argument.

articleTitle: Classification of Coadjoint Orbits for Symplectomorphism Groups of Surfaces
abstract: We classify generic coadjoint orbits for symplectomorphism groups of compact symplectic surfaces with or without boundary. We also classify simple Morse functions on such surfaces up to a symplectomorphism.

articleTitle: Overcrowding Estimates for the Nodal Volume of Stationary Gaussian Processes
abstract: For smooth centered stationary Gaussian processes on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathbb {R}}}^d$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d \geq 1$</tex>), we study the unlikely event of overcrowding of the nodal set; this is the event that the volume of the nodal set in a region is much larger than its expected value. Under some mild assumptions on the spectral measure of the process, we obtain estimates for the probability of the overcrowding event.

articleTitle: Arakelov Theory on Arithmetic Surfaces Over a Trivially Valued Field
abstract: In this article, we consider an analogue of Arakelov theory of arithmetic surfaces over a trivially valued field. In particular, we establish an arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel theorem and study the effectivity up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb R$</tex>-linear equivalence of pseudoeffective metrised <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb R$</tex>-divisors.
